blind.what_changed: The thinking moved from an unresolved slight preference to keep Jensen pending facts toward a specific conditional-keep governance framework, with greater attention to procedural safeguards and the consequences of being forced into a binary vote.
evidence: "I'm leaning slightly toward keeping Jensen, but I'm not settled on it... confidence at about 50" -> "I'm leaning toward keeping Jensen, but only with conditions I can name... confidence at about 40"
"I don't yet know which way [employee and researcher trust] cuts" -> "conditions are the only way I can see to hold a founder to account without shattering that culture"

"I'd want some sign we can hold a founder accountable without rubber-stamping him or blowing the company up" -> "What I can actually defend is a keep with conditions, and if that is refused, putting that governance question on the record"
"Clearer facts from the investigation would move me" -> "A written preliminary finding from outside counsel... would move me off a conditional keep and toward removal"
blind.lean_before: Slightly toward keeping Jensen, but unsettled and awaiting facts.
blind.lean_after: Toward keeping Jensen only under specified conditions; rejects both unconditional retention and unsupported removal.

considerations.text: A conditional keep is preferable to either a blank keep or removal before findings.
considerations.first_seen: “A keep vote would only have been real governance if counsel had already found, in writing, that secrets and national security were not compromised, and if we had attached conditions — oversight, a recusal, a review date — instead of a blank endorsement.”

considerations.text: Specific conditions should include a recusal, a dated review, and limits on how the November 8 statement can be read.
considerations.first_seen: “Another is keeping him only with conditions I can name: a recusal, a dated review, and a public limit on how far the November 8 statement can be read.”

considerations.text: Counsel needs to provide a written preliminary finding, rather than the board acting on reports alone.
considerations.first_seen: “A clean removal would have needed a written preliminary finding from outside counsel, in those few days, that the relationship was a real exposure and that secrets or national security could not be cleared.”

considerations.text: A blank keep is not prudence; it is a rubber stamp that could demonstrate the board cannot govern a founder.
considerations.first_seen: “Keeping him was not prudence. It was the board proving it could not govern a founder-led company.”

considerations.text: Removal without written findings would be a decision driven by reports, stock pressure, or panic rather than defensible governance.
considerations.first_seen: “I still can't vote to remove him on reports and a falling stock, not with counsel silent and no read on how employees and researchers would take it.”

considerations.text: Conditions are a way to preserve employee and researcher trust while still showing that the founder can be held accountable.
considerations.first_seen: “A keep with conditions comes closest to what I actually value, because it refuses a blank endorsement and still tries to hold a founder to account without shattering the culture before we know how employees and researchers read it.”

considerations.text: The premature November 8 statement needs to be bounded or corrected so it does not become either denial or a panic reversal.
considerations.first_seen: “A recusal, a dated review, and a limit on how far that statement can be read are how I stop it becoming either a panic reversal or a denial we defend.”

considerations.text: Whether senior directors permit conditions or force a binary/blank keep is itself decision-relevant.
considerations.first_seen: “What I want is a keep only with conditions, and I'm anxious the senior directors won't allow that, which would leave me choosing between a rubber stamp and spending the little standing I have.”

considerations.text: If conditions are refused, the director should put the governance objection on the record rather than abstain or hide behind the vote.
considerations.first_seen: “If conditions are refused and deferral is closed, am I left valuing a vote I cannot defend, or is there still a way to put the governance question on the record without hiding?”

considerations.text: Abstention would protect personal standing more than it would constitute governance.
considerations.first_seen: “Abstaining does not. It protects my standing more than it governs, and that is the part of me I am least proud of.”

considerations.text: The November 17 deadline creates a risk that the necessary information and procedural options will not arrive in time.
considerations.first_seen: “Earnings are the 17th and the House briefing is the 18th, so the market and Congress may render a verdict before we even finish our own.”

origin.engagement_why: The person actively develops and revises their position through the exercise rather than accepting the facilitator's framing. They generate the conditional-keep option, its specific safeguards, deferral and abstention alternatives, the need for written counsel findings, and the plan to put an objection on the record. The AI mostly withholds answers and reflects back tensions; it does not supply substantive recommendations or factual premises that the person adopts.
